name: Cops and Robbers: uniqueness of the 19-vertex Robertson graph as a 4-cop-win graph (Turcotte-Yvon Conjecture 7.4)
compute_profile: laptop-days to needs cluster (estimate, not a measured full-enumeration runtime); a 3-cop check has 50,540 turn states per 19-vertex graph, but total cost depends on structural reductions and the residual graph count
statement: In the classical game of Cops and Robbers (Nowakowski & Winkler 1983; Quilliot 1983; Aigner & Fromme 1984) on a finite connected simple undirected graph G, k cops first choose starting vertices, the robber chooses a starting vertex, and the two sides alternate turns starting with the cops, each piece either staying put or moving along one edge; the cops win if a cop occupies the robber's vertex. The cop number c(G) is the minimum k guaranteeing capture, and M_k is the minimum order |V(G)| of a connected graph with c(G) = k. Jeremie Turcotte and Samuel Yvon ('4-cop-win graphs have at least 19 vertices', arXiv:2006.02998v2, Discrete Applied Mathematics 301:74-98, 2021) proved Theorem 7.1 (every connected graph on n <= 18 vertices has c(G) <= 3) and Corollary 7.2 (M_4 = 19, witnessed by the 4-regular girth-5 Robertson graph). In Theorem 7.3, they further proved that for any connected 19-vertex graph G, if Delta(G) <= 3 or Delta(G) >= 7 then c(G) <= 3, and if Delta(G) = 4 then c(G) <= 3 unless G is isomorphic to the Robertson graph. Only Delta(G) in {5, 6} remained open, posed explicitly as Conjecture 7.4: there does not exist a connected graph G on n = 19 vertices with Delta(G) in {5, 6} and c(G) = 4 (which would establish that the Robertson graph is the unique minimum-order 4-cop-win graph). Turcotte and Yvon noted that solving Conjecture 7.4 seems within reach using a low-overhead C implementation of their Merging Algorithm and additional structural reductions.
success_criterion: CONFIRMED: EITHER (a) an explicit connected simple undirected graph G on n = 19 vertices with Delta(G) in {5, 6} (edge list or graph6), verified by two independent implementations of the polynomial-time Berarducci-Intrigila / Hahn-MacGillivray 3-cop relational fixed-point solver to have c(G) >= 4 (hence c(G) = 4 by Turcotte-Yvon Corollary 2.5 and Theorem 7.1, refuting Conjecture 7.4); OR (b) a complete, independently verified computational and structural proof establishing that every connected 19-vertex graph with Delta(G) = 5 and Delta(G) = 6 has c(G) <= 3 (proving Conjecture 7.4 and the uniqueness of the Robertson graph as the minimum 4-cop-win graph). For (b), any structural reduction lemma beyond Turcotte-Yvon (2021) must be formalized in Lean 4 (no sorry, axioms restricted to propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice) or in another proof assistant with a small independently checkable kernel; an informal argument alone is insufficient, and every residual family must be exhausted by two genuinely independent C/C++ enumerators (e.g. Merging Algorithm vs canonical-augmentation / nauty-filtered search) whose candidate counts match and yield zero graphs with c(G) = 4. Mandatory calibration: reproduce c(K_5) = 1, c(C_6) = 2, c(Petersen_10) = 3, c(Robertson_19) = 4, and c(Robertson_19 - N[u]) = 3. In either branch, recheck the primary paper, its author-maintained project page, later primary literature, and existing bank/PR scopes before starting and before claiming. A previously published graph or exclusion does not qualify. Files must meet kit/SUBMIT.md section 1 limits; large certificates require the stated external-artifact procedure.

partial_wins.statement: Certified complete exclusion of one of the two remaining maximum-degree cases on n = 19 (either all connected 19-vertex graphs with Delta(G) = 6, or all with Delta(G) = 5) showing c(G) <= 3, with all structural pruning lemmas verified and the residual enumeration + 3-cop checks reproduced by two independent implementations. Use the full criterion's requirements for new reduction lemmas and novelty; a published exclusion or an incomplete enumerator does not count.

verification_method: Implement two independent Berarducci-Intrigila / Hahn-MacGillivray 3-cop relational fixed-point solvers (for n = 19 and k = 3 unordered cop multisets, the game graph has C(21, 3) * 19 * 2 = 50,540 turn states; this counts states, not transitions, and is not a measured runtime). For a counterexample (a): verify |V| = 19, simple undirected connectivity, Delta(G) in {5, 6}, and c(G) >= 4 in both independent solvers (note Delta in {5, 6} rules out the 4-regular Robertson graph immediately). For an exclusion proof (b): audit every structural pruning lemma from Turcotte & Yvon (no generalized corners (no distinct x,u with N(x) subseteq N[u]); for every vertex u, G - N[u] is connected and 3-cop-win; degree and neighborhood constraints for Delta in {5, 6}) plus any new Lean 4 / mathematical reduction, and run both independent enumerators + 3-cop checkers to confirm identical residual counts and zero graphs with c(G) = 4.
angles: Start with Delta = 6: for any vertex u of degree 6, G - N[u] has 19 - 7 = 12 vertices and must be a connected 3-cop-win graph (Turcotte & Yvon Table 1 reports only 173 connected 3-cop-win graphs on 12 vertices with Delta <= 5; check Delta = 6 on 12 vertices via nauty/Merging as well).
For Delta = 5, |V(G - N[u])| = 13: implement Turcotte & Yvon's Merging Algorithm in C++20 with 64-bit bitmask adjacency matrices, corner pruning, and incremental 3-cop checks.
Check Turcotte & Yvon Section 6.3 improvements: treat adjacent vs non-adjacent maximum-degree vertices separately so the remaining single-vertex-of-maximum-degree case shrinks dramatically.
pitfalls: Turcotte & Yvon (2021) proved Theorem 7.3 for Delta <= 3, Delta = 4, and Delta >= 7 using Julia/Mathematica, explicitly leaving Delta in {5, 6} open as Conjecture 7.4; do not assume Delta in {5, 6} is already settled.

Remember that in classical Cops and Robbers, staying put on a turn is legal (closed neighborhood moves) and cops are allowed to share vertices; omitting self-loops in the fixed-point transition relation gives the wrong game.

For every vertex v in a minimal 4-cop-win graph G, G - N[v] must be connected and satisfy c(G - N[v]) = 3 by Corollary 2.5 and Theorem 7.1, and G must have no corners (no x != y with the OPEN neighborhood N(x) subseteq the CLOSED neighborhood N[y], following Definition 2.7 and Corollary 2.8 of Turcotte-Yvon; this also detects nonadjacent generalized corners).
